text: Given two calls share the same status/queueIDs/technicians combination and are issued so their counting steps would overlap without serialization, when both complete, then the second call's decision reflects the first call's result, not a stale snapshot -- the two calls never both pick the same technician off the same stale count
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 10 passed, 10 total (exit 0). Gates call A's Tickets/query to force a controlled overlap window with call B issued synchronously before any await; asserts call B's fetch calls only happen after the gate releases, and A picks R1 while B picks R2 (never the same resource).
note: r2: lock key changed from String(queueID) to a composite of status/queueIDs/technician resourceIDs (see PRD-20620-r2.md Tech design Key flow).

text: Given `technicians` is missing or an empty array, when a ticket is assigned, then the tool throws a distinct error (e.g. NoCandidateTechniciansError) and neither createTicket nor updateTicket is called
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 10 passed, 10 total (exit 0). Covers both `technicians` omitted and `technicians: []`; both return isError=true with the exact NoCandidateTechniciansError message, and asserts no POST /Tickets or PATCH /Tickets call ever happened.
note: r2: replaces round-1's 'zero eligible resources in a queue' case with 'technicians array missing/empty', since eligibility is now caller-supplied.

text: Given a technician has 10 total assigned tickets but only 2 match the given status/queueIDs filter, when counting that technician's load, then only the 2 matching tickets count toward their load -- the other 8 must not affect the selection
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 10 passed, 10 total (exit 0). Technician A has 2 matching + 8 non-matching-status + 1 wrong-queue tickets; asserts consideredTechnicians reports A=2 (not 10, not 3) and B=1, and the tool picks B.
note: r2: new case for the new status/queueIDs filtering requirement.

text: Given a successful assignment, when the tool returns its result, then `result` contains explicit typed fields for ticketID, assignedResourceID, assignedResourceRoleID, appliedFilter.status, appliedFilter.queueIDs, and consideredTechnicians[] (each with resourceID/roleID/matchingTicketCount) -- independent of what `message` says
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 10 passed, 10 total (exit 0). Asserts the exact shape: ticketID (number), assignedResourceID, assignedResourceRoleID (echoed from the chosen technician entry, not Autotask-resolved), appliedFilter === {status, queueIDs}, and consideredTechnicians as a typed array with resourceID/roleID/matchingTicketCount per entry.
note: r2: new case for the structured-output requirement ('传出的参数也需要结构化').

text: Given createTicket is used with queueIDs of length 0, and separately with length 2, when the tool is invoked, then both report a distinct validation error and no ticket is created
evidence: `npx jest assign-least-loaded` -> Tests: 10 passed, 10 total (exit 0). Covers queueIDs omitted and queueIDs with 2 entries, both with createTicket -> isError=true; also asserts the orthogonal case (ticketID reassignment, no createTicket) is unaffected by this rule (isError=false).
note: r2: new case -- queueIDs is now a counting filter (array, optional), so create-ticket needs its own rule for which single queue the new ticket lands in.

text: Given a live Autotask sandbox/INT environment with a real technicians list, when 5 test-prefixed tickets are created/reassigned through autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource with a real status/queueIDs filter, then the Autotask UI shows assignees spread per the least-matching-count rule and each assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID matches what the tool reported
steps: In INT/staging with real Autotask credentials, pick 3 or more real technicians (resourceID + roleID) and a real status/queueIDs combination
Call autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource 5 times with a clearly test-prefixed ticket title, passing the same technicians/status/queueIDs each time
Open the queue(s) in the Autotask UI and record each ticket's assignee and role
Compare against the tool's reported assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID for each call
expect: Assignees are spread (no single technician holds more than ceil(5/3)=2 of the 5 tickets) and the UI's assignee/role matches the tool's reported assignedResourceID/assignedResourceRoleID for every ticket
evidence: NOT EXECUTED: this sandbox has no AUTOTASK_USERNAME/AUTOTASK_SECRET credentials; needs dev/QA with live Autotask access after implementation. Same local blind spot as round 1's TC6/TC9, carried forward unchanged in substance (param shape updated to technicians/status/queueIDs).
